questions.stem: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution and are borrowed from which country?
options: Part IV; Ireland
Part III; the United States
Part IV-A; the USSR
Part IV; Australia
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Who described the Directive Principles as a 'novel feature' of the Indian Constitution, and which colonial instrument do they resemble?
options: B.R. Ambedkar; the Instrument of Instructions under the Government of India Act, 1935
Granville Austin; the Government of India Act, 1919
K.C. Wheare; the Charter Act of 1833
B.N. Rau; the Indian Councils Act, 1909
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The classification of DPSPs into Socialistic, Gandhian and Liberal-Intellectual principles is
options: made expressly by the Constitution itself
a scholarly classification not found in the Constitution
based on the Seventh Schedule
laid down by the Sardar Swaran Singh Committee
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: 'To organise village panchayats and endow them with powers to enable them to function as units of self-government' is a Directive Principle under which Article, and of which type?
options: Article 44; Liberal-Intellectual principle
Article 38; Socialistic principle
Article 40; Gandhian principle
Article 48; Gandhian principle
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following pairs of Directive Principle and its classification is correctly matched?
options: Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code) - Gandhian
Article 50 (separation of judiciary from executive) - Socialistic
Article 39A (free legal aid) - Liberal-Intellectual
Article 46 (promotion of educational and economic interests of weaker sections) - Gandhian
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following Directive Principles was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976?
options: Article 48A - protection and improvement of the environment
Article 44 - Uniform Civil Code
Article 40 - organisation of village panchayats
Article 50 - separation of judiciary from executive
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The subject matter of Article 45 was changed by the 86th Amendment, 2002 to focus on
options: free legal aid for the poor
early childhood care and education for children below the age of six years
a living wage for all workers
promotion of cottage industries
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a correct distinction between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles?
options: Fundamental Rights are non-justiciable; DPSPs are justiciable
Fundamental Rights aim at social democracy; DPSPs at political democracy
Fundamental Rights are justiciable and individualistic; DPSPs are non-justiciable and aim at the welfare of the community
Both have equal legal sanction and are enforceable in courts
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: In the event of a conflict, the general judicial position on Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is that
options: DPSPs always prevail over Fundamental Rights
DPSPs can never be given effect if a Fundamental Right is affected
both are equally enforceable and courts must balance them case by case with binding force
Fundamental Rights generally prevail, but Parliament may amend them to implement DPSPs without damaging the basic structure
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Uniform Civil Code is a Directive Principle under which Article, and which States have implemented it?
options: Article 44; Goa and Uttarakhand
Article 44; Kerala and Tamil Nadu
Article 48; Goa and Gujarat
Article 50; Assam and Nagaland
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by which amendment, on the recommendation of which committee?
options: 44th Amendment; Santhanam Committee
42nd Amendment; Sardar Swaran Singh Committee
86th Amendment; Sarkaria Commission
52nd Amendment; Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were inspired by the Constitution of
options: the United States
Ireland
the erstwhile USSR
Japan
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: How many Fundamental Duties are there at present, and which one was added later?
options: Ten; all added in 1976
Eleven; a duty to vote added by the 61st Amendment
Twelve; a duty to pay taxes added in 2002
Eleven; the duty on education (6-14 years) added by the 86th Amendment, 2002
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee was NOT accepted while incorporating Fundamental Duties?
options: To provide for a penalty for non-compliance and a duty to pay taxes
To cherish the ideals of the freedom struggle
To respect the National Flag and the National Anthem
To protect the natural environment
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about Fundamental Duties is correct?
options: They are available to both citizens and foreigners
They are restricted to citizens and are non-justiciable, though Parliament may enforce them by law
They are directly enforceable in courts
They were part of the original Constitution of 1950
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Fundamental Duty to 'protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife and to have compassion for living creatures' is contained in
options: Article 48A
Article 21A
Article 51A(g)
Article 39A
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: 'To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform' is
options: a Directive Principle of State Policy
a Fundamental Right
a Preambular objective
a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A?
options: To promote village and cottage industries
To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To value and preserve the rich heritage of the composite culture
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Directive Principle that directs the State to 'separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State' is
options: Article 48
Article 50
Article 51
Article 39A
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: 'To promote international peace and security and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration' is a Directive Principle under
options: Article 44
Article 48A
Article 51
Article 43B
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following was added as a Fundamental Duty through the Constitution 86th Amendment Act, 2002?
options: To strive towards excellence in individual and collective activity
To provide opportunities for education to one's child between the age of 6 and 14 years
To work for the welfare of women and children
To promote peace and harmony
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Part IV-A of the Constitution of India deals with which one of the following areas?
options: Appointment of Members to Public Service Commissions
Fundamental Duties
Functions of Public Service Commissions
Provisions for the functioning of the State Governments
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: In Part IV-A of the Constitution of India, which one of the following is NOT mentioned as a duty of every citizen of India?
options: To render national service when called upon to do so
To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women
To value and preserve a unitary national culture
To develop the spirit of inquiry and reform
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a part of Article 51 of the Constitution of India?
options: Promote international peace and security
Maintain just and honourable relations between nations
Use of UN peacekeeping force for resolution of international disputes
Encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: According to the provisions of the Constitution of India, which one of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?
options: To respect the National Flag
To defend the country
To provide education to one's child
To promote village and cottage industries
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which case held that the balance and harmony between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is itself part of the basic structure of the Constitution?
options: Champakam Dorairajan (1951)
A.K. Gopalan (1950)
Golaknath (1967)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following DPSPs is Gandhian in character?
options: Article 47 - prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs
Article 41 - right to work and public assistance
Article 39A - free legal aid
Article 51 - promotion of international peace
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about the Uniform Civil Code (Article 44) is correct?
options: It is a Fundamental Right of every Indian citizen
It is a non-justiciable Directive Principle that the State shall endeavour to secure
It is enforceable by the courts
It applies automatically without any legislation
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly pairs a constitutional provision with the environment?
options: Both are Fundamental Rights
Article 48A - Fundamental Duty; Article 51A(g) - Directive Principle
Article 48A - Directive Principle on the State; Article 51A(g) - Fundamental Duty on citizens
Both are Directive Principles
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about the enforceability of DPSPs is correct?
options: Courts can strike down a law solely for violating a DPSP
DPSPs are enforceable exactly like Fundamental Rights
DPSPs are enforceable only in High Courts, not the Supreme Court
Courts cannot enforce DPSPs but may use them to test and uphold the validity of a law
questions.subject: Polity
